messages:
Sam: Quick sync: prototype idea - control plane issues short-lived HMAC 'admit tickets' for fastpath, operator verifies and consumes local tokens. Aim: keep operator simple and avoid global RPCs on each request.

Kai: Nice. How short-lived? signing cost?

Sam: Default 30s expiry, HMAC verify only, no public-key ops. Ticket fields: tenant, lane, gpu_ms, issued_at, expires_at, nonce.

Anya: Replay risk? tiny-request spam?

Priya: Use min_gpu_ms and per-tenant concurrency caps. Operator keeps small LRU nonce cache to reject replays and enforces a local token-bucket.

Sam: Credits: long-term ledger in control plane (hourly), short-lived burst balance with fast decay (~10m half-life). Admin API to inject credits for emergencies.

Kai: Placement fallback?

Sam: Operator-local admission preferred. If shard free > X% try async cross-shard placemanager; else return fail so control plane can issue fallback tickets (quantized or lower-batch).

Anya: Observability: metrics needed: ticket_accepted, ticket_replayed, ticket_expired, local_bucket_fill, node_spinups, prewarm_count, admit_latency. Traces for ticket life.

Priya: Tests: nonce replay, expiry, HMAC mismatch, slow boot chaos. Also require min_gpu_ms=200 for burst.

orch-bot: build:operator-shim v0.2 pushed to staging (sha:def456). unit tests: ticket verification passing.

Sam: Owners: Priya (ledger + reconciliation), Kai (operator shim + nonce cache), Anya (metrics/tracing). I'll draft RFC follow-up and proto PR.
